content: Burt's Bees is a company that focuses on creating environmentally friendly and natural personal care products. Their product range includes items for personal care, health, beauty, and hygiene. As of 2007, the company produces over 150 products, including those for facial and body skincare, lip care, hair care, baby care, men's grooming, and outdoor remedies. These products are distributed in approximately 30,000 retail locations across the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. The company is headquartered in Durham, North Carolina. Each product features a natural bar, which indicates the percentage of natural ingredients it contains, often accompanied by detailed descriptions of the ingredients. This philosophy is reflected in their use of natural ingredients, environmentally sustainable practices, and community-focused humanitarian efforts. The company originated in Maine during the 1980s as a small business selling honey. Over time, they expanded their offerings to include products made from honey and beeswax, such as edible spreads and furniture polish, before transitioning into personal care products. Their product categories now include face care (cleansers, exfoliants, toners, moisturizers, skin treatments, and eye creams), lip care (lip balms, glosses, and shimmers), body care (body washes, soaps, moisturizers, and bath oils), hand care (soaps and moisturizers), foot care (creams, lotions, and pumice stones), hair care (shampoos, conditioners, and treatments), baby care (washes, soaps, diaper care, and moisturizers), pregnant mother care (belly moisturizers, leg and foot creams, and baby oils), men's grooming (body washes, soaps, shaving products, moisturizers, and colognes), and sun and outdoor care (sunscreens, lip balms, skin protection, and irritation products). Burt's Bees products are available in both regular and sample sizes and are sold in natural and specialty food markets such as Trader Joe's and Whole Foods Market. In 2005, the products became available in traditional pharmacy chains like CVS and Walgreens, as well as in Target and Borders Books outlets. The company was founded in 1984 as a candle-making partnership between Roxanne Quimby and Burt Shavitz. Shavitz's honey business provided the beeswax needed for the candles, and Quimby's dedication to quality helped the business grow from an initial $200 in sales at a craft fair to $20,000 by the end of the first year. Their first headquarters was an abandoned one-room schoolhouse rented for $150 per year. Production increased significantly after a New York boutique, Zona, placed a large order for their beeswax candles. This led to the hiring of 40 additional employees and a move to an abandoned bowling alley for manufacturing. During this time, Quimby discovered a 19th-century book of homemade personal care recipes, which inspired the company to enter the personal care industry. Burt's Bees eventually incorporated and expanded its product line to include candles, natural soaps, perfumes, and lip balm, which became their best-selling product. Quimby later bought out Shavitz's shares in the company. As demand grew, the company relocated its headquarters from Maine to North Carolina, where other personal care product manufacturers were based. The new manufacturing facility was an 18,000-square-foot former garment factory in Creedmoor, North Carolina. Despite the introduction of automated machines, such as a cafeteria mixer from Duke University, the company maintained its homemade product theme. The first Burt's Bees retail store opened in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, offering 50 natural personal care products. The company's distribution expanded to the Japanese market, and by this time, Burt's Bees was offering over 100 natural personal care products in 4,000 locations, with sales exceeding $8 million. Their products were also being sold in high-end national retailers like Whole Foods Market and Cracker Barrel. The company introduced travel-sized skincare and hair care products and relocated to Durham, North Carolina, to accommodate increasing demand and a growing product line, which included sugarand milk-based body lotions and bath products. An eCommerce website was launched, enabling nationwide distribution. Burt's Bees introduced its first toothpaste, shampoo, and the successful Baby Bee product line for infant care. Founder Roxanne Quimby used company profits to preserve 185,000 acres of forest land in Maine, initiating a partnership with The Nature Conservancy, an international environmental protection organization. In 2003, private equity firm AEA Investors purchased 80% of Burt's Bees, with Quimby retaining a 20% share and a seat on the board. Michael Indursky, a former executive at Garnier and Unilever, joined the company in 2005 to lead marketing and public relations. In 2006, John Replogle, a former general manager of Unilever's skincare division, became the CEO and President of Burt's Bees. Replogle had previously held leadership roles at Guinness and Diageo. As of 2006, Burt's Bees offered over 150 natural personal care products in 30,000 retail locations, with sales exceeding $250 million. The company also maintained satellite offices in the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.
